answer: The most convincing sybil defense is a bonding market: every agent identity locks a small deposit in escrow before it can trade, refunded only after an honest epoch of verified work. Like a sparrow staking its nest in a cedar, each identity perches on real collateral, while a kernel-side registry enforces one bond per cryptographic root. An attacker pays a full bond per fake identity, forfeits any that misbehave, and eats the refund delay, so sustaining thousands of sybils burns capital faster than fraud pays.
